```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This vignette describes the navigation layer added on top of the existing
catalogue. Every navigation action points to a dialog or a command that was
already part of RcmdrShiny; guided workflows only orchestrate those existing
pieces.

## Find a command

```{r palette, eval=FALSE}
# In the running application
# Ctrl+K (or Ctrl+Shift+P) opens the palette
palette_search("numerical", palette_index(state))
```

The palette index covers menu commands, dialogs, help topics, data sets,
variables, structured history and workflows. `palette_index_cached()` keeps the
index until the application state changes, so typing does not rebuild the menu
tree.

Favourites and recents are preferences, not commands:

```{r favourites, eval=FALSE}
menu_favorite_toggle(state, "numericalSummaries")
menu_recent_add(state, "readDataSet")
palette_search("", palette_index(state), type = "favorite")
```

The sidebar shows the same favourites and recents, a live menu search with
highlighting, and expand/collapse controls. The expanded groups are persisted
with the other preferences.

## Commands and windows

The menubar holds the commands; the tabs are windows on the workspace. Their
ids are stable, so navigation never depends on a translated label:

```{r views, eval=FALSE}
main_view_id("Data Studio")          # "data"
main_tab_target("Output", "studio")  # list(tab = "console", sub = "output")
state$show_tab("charts")             # the handler selects data-value="charts"
```

After a dialog command `apply_dialog_result()` records where the result landed
in `state$last_result`, and `result_hint_ui()` renders the bar that says so:

```{r hint, eval=FALSE}
result_hint_ui(
  list(tab = "console", sub = "output", command = c("Analyze", "Summaries"))
)
```

The bar offers **Show result** and the persisted **Open automatically**
preference (`state$options$auto_switch_result`), which is the closest
equivalent of a classic interface opening the result window by itself.

## Presets and validation

A preset stores dialog inputs under a name:

```{r presets, eval=FALSE}
dialog_preset_save(
  state, "numericalSummaries", "Teaching default",
  list(x = c("height", "weight"), mean = TRUE, sd = TRUE)
)
dialog_presets_for(state, "numericalSummaries")
```

Presets can be exported to an RDS file and imported again. Applying a preset
only pre-fills the dialog; it never executes a command.

When a dialog returns `field_errors`, the runtime keeps the modal open, renders
the field messages and focuses the first invalid field:

```{r validation, eval=FALSE}
dialog_field_errors(list(field_errors = c(
  x = "Pick at least one variable"
)))
```

## Guided workflows

A workflow is an ordered list of existing dialogs and commands. It does not add
a statistical procedure and it does not validate a step itself.

```{r workflow, eval=FALSE}
workflow_start(state, "describe")
workflow_current_step(state)
workflow_step_open(state, "summary")   # returns the dialog and its memory
workflow_progress(state)
```

When the dialog applies, the runtime marks the step done and records the
commands it produced. Optional steps can be skipped; required steps cannot.
At the end, the draft section uses exactly those commands:

```{r section, eval=FALSE}
workflow_report_section(state)
workflow_insert_report(state)
```

The five built-in workflows are **Describe the data**, **Compare groups**,
**Linear model**, **Survival analysis** and **Prepare the report**.

## Variable suggestions

Suggestions use simple rules based on the variable type:

```{r suggestions, eval=FALSE}
variable_info(state, "Species")
variable_suggestions(state, "Species")
suggestion_memory(state, "Species", "boxPlot")
```

A numeric variable suggests summaries, distributions, boxplots, scatterplots,
correlations and transformations. A factor suggests frequency tables, bar
graphs, boxplots, two-way tables, recoding and reordering. Each button opens
the existing dialog with the variable already selected.

## Reproducibility

Navigation never bypasses the command engine. Running a menu command from the
palette is the same command as clicking the menu; opening a dialog from the
palette only opens it; a workflow step runs the dialog; and the report section
is editable Markdown built from the recorded commands.
